## Runs 6–7 — raw spot checks, frequency candidates, and onset limitation

`sdh-spot-check`, investigation Steps 2–3: sr1 is the sole connected voltage pair B_1–B_2; sr0 measures drain current. Raw signed Rxx is shown before FFT; no positive-value clipping or log transform is used. Both runs are complete, unrailed (|R| < 590 Ohm versus 5 kOhm nominal full scale), with drain current 9.81–9.94 nA, sample T 1.165–1.292 K, and maximum absolute TG/BG currents below 216/121 pA.

Electron run 6 (n_A=+3.2e12, D_A≈0) has candidate frequencies near 7, 14, 22 and 29 T, stable between degree-3 and degree-5 detrenders above 1 T; the 7/22/29 set permits a partition plus sum-tone explanation, but harmonics and density-inhomogeneity remain unresolved. No stacking assignment follows from this one column. Hole run 7 (n_A=-1.2e12) has ~5–7 T and ~12 T features; the gate-limited hole window is in the model's near-CNP ambiguity regime. The two CNP ridges in run 5 are spatial-inhomogeneity evidence, not proof of different stacking.

The default electron onset estimator is **censored at 0.30 T**; below 1 T, the 50 mT acquisition spacing also undersamples F_L=33.1 T. Restricting the background-fit upper edge to 4–5 T gives the ~6.8 T tone an onset 1.02–1.04 T, whereas the full 10 T background extrapolation produces low-field residual tones. This extraction dependence must be resolved before committing the fan; a short fine-grid low-field check is the next step. Positive-B data only: even-in-B symmetrization is unavailable, so Hall admixture remains a caveat. Absolute density scale remains geometry-prior; the fan must fit one global scale to the whole peak set and compare both ABAB and adjacent-N templates.

from pathlib import Path
import json
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from hera.analysis import open_run, plot_raw, resolve_channels, current_channel, sdh_onset, sdh_fft
out={}
for rid,n in [(6,3.2),(7,-1.2)]:
    run=open_run(Path('data')/str(rid))
    fig=plot_raw(run); plt.savefig(f'hera_scratch/spot_{rid}_raw.png'); plt.show()
    ch=resolve_channels(run.meta); cur=current_channel(ch); v=next(c for c in ch if c.cid=='sr1')
    I=run.col(cur.col)/cur.gain; R=(run.col(v.col)/v.gain)/I; B=run.col('magnet_field')
    order=np.argsort(B); B,R=B[order],R[order]
    on=sdh_onset(R,B,r_full_scale=5000)
    print(f'RUN {rid} n={n}:',on.summary())
    print('R range',R.min(),R.max(),'I nA',I.min()*1e9,I.max()*1e9,'T',run.col('T_sample').min(),run.col('T_sample').max())
    print('gate max pA',*[np.max(np.abs(run.col(c)))*1e12 for c in ['k_2400_tg_curr','k_2400_bg_curr']])
    fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4)); ax[0].plot(B,R); ax[0].axvline(on.onset_b,color='r'); ax[0].set(xlabel='B (T)',ylabel='Rxx (Ohm)',title=f'Run {rid}: raw signed Rxx')
    peaks={}
    for lo in [on.onset_b,1.,1.5,2.]:
        if lo>=9: continue
        for deg in [3,5]:
            f,sp=sdh_fft(R[:,None],B,b_range=(lo,10),bg_degree=deg,log=False,nfft=4096)
            pk,_=find_peaks(sp[0]); pk=[p for p in pk if 2<f[p]<60]; pk=sorted(pk,key=lambda p:-sp[0,p])[:6]
            peaks[f'{lo:.3f}/{deg}']=[round(float(f[p]),2) for p in pk]
            ax[1].plot(f,sp[0]/sp[0].max(),label=f'B>{lo:.2f}, deg {deg}')
    ax[1].axvline(10.33916924*abs(n),color='k',ls='--',label='F_L scale 1'); ax[1].set(xlim=(0,60),xlabel='F (T)',ylabel='normalized FFT'); ax[1].legend(fontsize=6)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f'hera_scratch/spot_{rid}_fft.png'); plt.show()
    print('FFT peak candidates:',peaks)
    out[str(rid)]={'onset':on.onset_b,'summary':on.summary(),'peaks':peaks}
json.dump(out,open('hera_scratch/spot_results.json','w'),indent=2)

## Run 6 — onset cross-check and committed fan design

The full-record onset is sensitive to the large high-field magnetoresistance background. Across upper limits 4 and 5 T and polynomial degrees 3–5, the tracked ~6.7–6.8 T tone dies off at **1.018–1.040 T**, uncensored; it is marginal in the 4 T/degree-3,4 fits but robust in all 5 T fits. The default `sdh_onset(..., b_hi=5, r_full_scale=5000)` returns **1.0176178808 T**. The censored 0.3 T headline in the original full-record analysis is therefore not used as a physical onset. This cross-check supplies the fan's low edge without another sweep; the earlier proposed low-field extension is superseded. The 50 mT sub-1-T sampling cannot establish absence of fast tones there; the fan makes no such absence claim.

Commit one ascending `landau-fan-vti`: n_A=+2.7…+3.2e12 cm^-2 at D_A=0, B=1.0176178808…9.2 T, 120 uniform-1/B rows × 14 paired gate points. The ABAB forward model (input density in m^-2) gives light/heavy frequencies 5.721/22.190 T at n=2.7 and 7.306/25.783 T at n=3.2. At the low edge this provides 5.000 periods of the nominal partner and δF=1.144 T; the dominant-tone/singleton separation 5.721 T exceeds 2δF. The 0.5e12 density span measures branch motion while avoiding the low-density ABAB singleton trap. Five-period reach is nominal: a revised absolute density scale can reduce it, and that will limit the verdict rather than be hidden.

The mesh includes 20% density-scale headroom and the run-5 second-ridge offset 0.43e12 for sampling: F_max=45.037 T, Δ(1/B)=0.0073445 T^-1 (3.02 samples/period; Nyquist 68.1 T), Δn=0.03846e12 (2.13 samples per worst-case g=4 ray at B_lo). Strong ~59 T second harmonics are sampled; higher harmonics must still be screened by grid reproduction and B-window tests. The spectra and model overlays, rather than an assumed harmonic ratio, will decide the interpretation. Higher-order high-B structure and unknown polarized phases are outside this design guarantee.

The calculation uses the run-5 gate-current NPLC=1 timing (1.102 s/pt at 1 s dwell) and preserves the spot-check 3 s settling (10τ at 24 dB/oct). Allow 3.25 s/pt for paired gate ramps, added readbacks, and guards: 1680×3.25 s = 91.0 min, plus 9.2/0.137=67.2 min field travel from handoff zero and 120×7.5 s = 15 min turnaround, then 15% contingency ≈ **3 h 20 min**. A full -1.2…+3.2 window at this same mesh would cost approximately 16–17 h and still fail the five-period model-partner requirement at low electron density; it is excluded. Hole-side evidence remains run 7, and sr2/sr3 are disconnected. No region-resolved stacking verdict is yet justified; only B_1–B_2 is observed, with unresolved spatial mixing suggested by the two CNP ridges.

## HERA — D≈0 electron Landau fan for the stacking investigation

> **05:25** · D=0 electron fan: n=+2.7..+3.2e12 cm^-2; B 1.018->9.2 T; 120 uniform-1/B x 14 paired gates; base T; 10 nA; 3 s dwell; sr1 50 uV · **ETA ~08:45** (≈3h20m)

`landau-fan-vti` under `tetralayer-stacking-fs-count` Steps 4–5. Gate A/B and the E1 grant remain valid (measure cells 18, 32, 44–46); Gate C passed in runs 0–3. Run 5 provides the gate calibration, and the raw/FFT/onset analyses of both spot checks are in ana cells 14–17. Run 6 has ~7,22,29 T candidates whose density trajectories can separate pockets, harmonics, and sum tones. Choose the electron side because the accessible hole side remains in the model's near-CNP ambiguity regime. Only sr1/B_1–B_2 probes a connected region; the two CNP ridges imply unresolved spatial inhomogeneity, not two assigned stacking domains.

**Coverage and mesh.** n_A=+2.7…+3.2e12 cm^-2, D_A=0, B=1.0176178808→9.2 T, 120 uniform-1/B rows × 14 paired gate points (1680 samples). TG=0.84034…0.98359 V; BG=0.98090…1.16628 V, all inside the unchanged card validators. The low edge comes from `sdh_onset` on run 6 with `b_hi=5`: the ~6.8 T tone's uncensored onset is 1.018–1.040 T across 4–5 T upper windows and degrees 3–5. The full 10 T polynomial creates a censored low-field residual; its 0.3 T headline is not used. The earlier low-field-extension idea is superseded by this cross-check. No fast-tone absence claim below 1 T is possible from run 6.

**Feasibility.** The ABAB forward model gives partner/heavy frequencies 5.721/22.190 T at n=2.7 and 7.306/25.783 T at n=3.2; F_L is 27.916…33.089 T. The 1/B span 0.8740 T^-1 yields δF=1.144 T and 5.000 nominal partner periods at n_min. The singleton/heavy separation exceeds 2δF. B_max=9.2 T is the first 0.1 T increment meeting the five-period requirement for this density window. Sampling includes 20% global-scale uncertainty plus the run-5 0.43e12 second-ridge offset: F_max=45.04 T, Δ(1/B)=0.0073445 T^-1 (3.02 samples/period; Nyquist 68.1 T), Δn=0.03846e12 (2.13 samples per worst-case g=4 ray). Strong ~59 T second harmonics are sampled; higher harmonics and flavor polarization require an explicit audit. Five-period coverage is nominal and must be recalculated after the global density-scale fit. The fan's restricted density span limits adjacent-N discrimination and does not promise a definitive stacking call.

**Coverage trade.** Lower electron densities fail the five-period partner requirement within the 10 T cap and approach the ABAB-singleton ambiguity; holes reach only -1.27e12 on this D line. A -1.2…+3.2 fan at the same sampling would cost about 16–17 h while retaining those ambiguities. Keep run 7 as the hole-side evidence. The chosen window gives a 0.5e12 cross-density test; no conclusions outside it are implied.

**Timing and range.** Keep the spot-check 3 s settle (10τ, τ=0.3 s, 24 dB/oct), 10 nA drive, and fixed sr1 sensitivity 50 µV (5 kOhm full scale). Run-6 max R=530 Ohm at n=3.2; allow a conservative fivefold low-n MR increase and 3.2/2.7 scaling, 3.14 kOhm, with a 90%-FS stop guard. Run 5 measured 1.102 s/pt at 1 s dwell/NPLC=1. Budget 3.25 s/pt for paired ramps/additional readbacks: 91 min acquisition + 9.2/0.137=67.2 min total field travel from handoff zero (7.4 min initial positioning) + 15 min turnaround, with 15% contingency. The scan ascends once and holds at its endpoint for the next deliberate move.

**Preconditions and checkpoints.** The cell prints and checks all validators, fresh sample/vaporizer logs, base T, heaters off, measured B≈0, Si=0/RNGE2/output-on, hardwired routing, lock-in timing/drive, NPLC=1 and unchanged gate pacing before any write. Every acquired channel is live-plotted. Inspect the first three complete rows (~12 min including positioning), then every 20 rows or 30 min: leakage, current delivery, rails, temperature/freshness, measured B, and channel liveness. Per-point guards stop for the existing 1 nA gate-current threshold, rail approach, temperature/current/readback anomalies; freshness is checked each row. Stop and drop to E0 on a safety anomaly. On this VTI, kernel interrupt does **not** halt a magnet ramp already in progress: operator action at the supply is required for a ramp emergency; re-read actual state after any interrupt.

**Read after completion.** Raw native-grid Rxx first, then per-column FFT/window and detrending checks, one global density scale fitted to the whole peak set, ABAB/ABCA and mandatory adjacent-N overlays. Screen harmonics using density trajectories and partition sums; compare low/high-B windows before any F_L singleton/domain claim. Record the region-limited verdict and unresolved forks in ana. No automatic heater step or close-out is included.
